newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan August trade surplus up 17.8 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan August trade surplus up 17.8 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan had a trade surplus of US$1.129 billion in August, up 17.8 percent from a surplus of US$957.8 million in August 1995, the finance ministry said on Saturday.
The following is a table of trade figures in millions of U.S. dollars:
August 1996 August 1995
Exports 9,723 9,868
Imports 8,595 8,910
Trade balance +1,129 +958
August imports and exports both declined from August 1995, and the ministry attributed the year-on-year increase in the surplus to a slower decline in exports than that for imports.

"Because of slower growth in global trade and the tensions between Taiwan and China, the cumulative exports in the first eight months of 1996 grew only 3.5 percent compared with a year earlier," the ministry said in a statement.
"Exports to Hong Kong grew an annual 8.1 percent in August compared to a decline of 9.1 percent in July," it said, calling the jump the largest this year for exports to Hong Kong.
"Trade with Hong Kong is expected to be alive again."
The ministry said the outlook for Taiwan's trade was good.

"In the future, with the easing of tension across the Taiwan strait and gradual recovery of domestic investment and private consumption, we can expect higher growth of our imports and exports," the statement said.
The United States was Taiwan's biggest export destination in August. Exports to the United States fell 4.8 percent to $2.357 billion, or 24.2 percent of the monthly total.
Exports to Hong Kong rose 8.1 percent to $2.242 billion while those to Japan fell 9.3 percent to $1.082 billion, comprising 23.1 percent and 11.1 percent, respectively.
Exports to Europe fell an annual 6.6 percent to $1.314 billion, representing 13.5 percent of the total.
Imports from the United States rose 2.2 percent to $1.72 billion, or 20 percent of total August imports.
Taiwan's August trade surplus with the United States was $637 million, down 19.7 percent from August 1995.
The surplus with Hong Kong rose 9.7 percent to $2.108 billion from August 1995.
The deficit with Japan was down 23.5 percent to $1.103 billion, while the deficit with Europe fell 10.1 percent to $308 million.
-- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
